content:
arjun: Quick check — can we run a focused microbench + quality sweep for redwood-7b-v2 under hybrid int4+fp8 profiles? Trying to validate tail-latency and hallucination delta before we flip canary.

sana: yep, can do. which load shape and prompts?

arjun: light burst pattern (p50~~20ms target), steady background qps ~120rps. Use promptset `qc/2026/summary-lite` + 1000 open-ended prompts for hallucination stats.

mike: pinging bench infra. I can schedule GPU pool A (4xA100) for a 2h run tonight. ops, any capacity constraints?

ops: Pool A has a maintenance window 03:30-04:00 UTC, otherwise clear. Schedule outside that window.

lisa: quick note — add KV-cache warmup step, else int4 tails blow up. Recommend warmup=32 per worker.

arjun: good call. add `--kv-warmup 32`. also request p99, p995, and 99th token latency breakdown.

eng-bench-bot: job created: JB-2148, config: model=redwood-7b-v2, variant=hybrid-int4-fp8, batch=16, seq=2048, warmup=32, prompts=qc/2026/summary-lite (1000). ETA 2h. link: https://bench/reports/JB-2148

mike: starting job now, will post interim perf snapshot at +30m. cc @sana for quality hooks.

(30m later)
mike: interim perf snapshot: p50=18.6ms, p90=39.2ms, p99=112.5ms, p995=210.4ms. throughput ~118 rps.

arjun: thanks — p99 is 112, ok but p995 high. need tail profiling. can we get a flame + kernel breakdown?

mike: grabbing traces, enabling per-kernel counters. will attach logs.

(attachments: small stacklog snippet pasted inline)
mike: ```
kv_cache_miss_pct: 12.3
matmul_kernel_avg_ms: 4.1
attention_kernel_avg_ms: 28.7
io_wait_ms: 0.8
context_switch_ms: 0.2
```

arjun: attention dominates as expected for long seqs. is fp8 path introducing extra quant rescale overhead?

kyle: I ran a micro profile yesterday — hybrid fp8 path has a +0.6ms/step rescale in attention but reduces matmul by ~1.2ms due to lower memory bandwidth. net usually wins for throughput but can spike tail when KV misses + long attention.

sana: quality quick check results (from `qc/2026/summary-lite`): baseline fp16: hallucination rate 0.9%, chrBLEU ~ 87.6. hybrid-int4-fp8: hallucination 1.6%, chrBLEU 86.1. top-level regressions concentrated on numeric precision prompts (tables) and rare entity hallucinations.

arjun: delta hallucination +0.7% is borderline. need to see if can tune quantization scale or fallback policy for low-confidence tokens.

lisa: suggestion: enable fallback-to-fp16 on confidence<0.7 for logits of numeric tokens. Also try mixed-origin KV cache (store fp8, serve fp16 for hot keys) — quick experiment.

mike: can run an A/B canary: 90% hybrid-int4-fp8, 10% fp16 for 1h over the same prompt set and measure per-prompt regressed fraction. want me to kick that now?

arjun: yes. schedule after current job completes. set alert if hallucination delta >0.5% or p995>250ms.

eng-bench-bot: job JB-2148 completed. report: https://bench/reports/JB-2148/summary
eng-bench-bot: spawned AB-2149 for canary A/B with 90/10 split. ETA 1.5h.

(1h later)
eng-bench-bot: AB-2149 interim: hybrid-int4-fp8: hallucination 1.58%, fp16: 0.91%. regressed prompts (by id): [234,512,689,912] — mostly numeric tables. perf snapshot hybrid: p99=118ms, p995=220ms. fp16: p99=120ms, p995=215ms.

arjun: interesting — perf roughly similar; quality worse on hybrid for those prompt types. maybe quant scale tweak needed for numeric tokens.

sana: I'll run targeted quant calibration on numeric tokens (scale+offset) and re-run 200-case focused sweep. give me 2h.

kyle: small note — if we add selective fp16 fallback per-token, it could increase tail slightly. need to measure combination effects.

arjun: agreed. plan: 1) sana runs calibration + focused 200-case sweep, 2) mike runs a 4h stability run with fallback policy enabled (conf<0.7 -> fp16 numeric fallback), 3) ops confirm no maintenance during 4h window. we'll reconvene in ~6h with results. :eyes: 

lisa: capturing action items in RT board. arjun -> follow up on rollout gating doc.

arjun: thanks — if calibration moves hallucination delta below 0.4% and p995 stays <240ms, we'll proceed with a slow ramp canary. otherwise hold.

mike: ack, scheduling runs.

sana: starting calibration now, will post a short diff and sample outputs when done.

arjun: great — appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
